verses.text: The word “skillful” appears about 24 times in late-19th to early-20th-century editions of the Douay-Rheims Bible. In other 19th-century editions which were printed from Irish printing plates (such as those by M. H. Hill & Son or Robert & Daniel Read, or American reprints by the Benzinger Brothers), it was spelled as “skilful” with only one L. The 1611 King James Version also has it as “skilful” with one L, because this was the standard spelling at the time, and is retained as the European or British spelling until today. John Murphy Press changed the spelling to “skillful” with two Ls for their 1899 Baltimore edition to make it more akin to modern American English; although some American editions from the 20th century, such as a 1914 reprint of the Douay-Rheims Bible by P. J. & Sons, retained the British spelling. (See Genesis 11:3 for more.)
